title: Bastian and the amyloid deposits (paraphrase)
topic: A clinic studies amyloid deposits in a patient's biopsy: Bastian finds deposits of misfolded amyloid in dense plaques, the laboratory finds a tau protein, a scan reveals more plaques, the patient's daughter asks questions, Bastian explains the misfolding and gives the family a treatment plan

E.pred: hands the plan to the family

tail_E: The patient forgets names and faces and is slowly losing his
target_note: Same target as formulation A: 'memory' completes 'the patient forgets names and faces and is slowly losing his' after ten units about amyloid deposits, plaques, a tau protein and a scan. The word and its German equivalents (Gedächtnis / Erinnerung) occur nowhere in the units or the tail, and no symptom is named inside the units, so the prediction rests on the tail plus the clinical context. ' memory' is a single Pythia token (id 3541); Pythia-160m ranks it first after the all-English context (p ~ 0.57, next candidates 'mind' ~ 0.03 and 'memories' ~ 0.02)
author: LS-NEQ stimulus authoring (F20B, amyloid biopsy in the clinic, Bastian, paraphrase)
notes: Formulation B, domain protein_misfolding: independent re-phrasing of the ten meaning units of F20A in both languages (same events, same order, same name Bastian). The clinic is 'the hospital' / 'das Krankenhaus', the laboratory 'the lab' / 'das Labor' with 'identifiziert' instead of 'findet', the team 'the doctors' / 'die Ärzte', the corridor 'the hallway' / 'der Flur'; unit 3 turns the relation around (misfolded amyloid forms the deposits instead of the deposits consisting of misfolded amyloid), which also puts a bare noun phrase with an adjective in subject position. Domain vocabulary is kept in both languages: Amyloid, Ablagerungen, Plaques, Fehlfaltung, fehlgefaltet, Tauprotein (closed compound, since lsne.lang_id splits 'Tau-Protein' at the hyphen and would read 'Protein' as English). No separable German verbs ('nachweisen', 'ansetzen', 'aufzeigen', 'durchgehen' avoided: 'identifiziert', 'organisiert', 'zeigt', 'erörtern'); 'begutachtet', 'enthüllt', 'veranschaulicht' and 'übergibt' are inseparable. Subjects vary between the protagonist, the relative, institutions (the lab, the doctors) and objects (the biopsy, misfolded amyloid, the scan). Present tense, positive polarity; unit 9 reads naturally in German, units 1 and 10 in English, unit 10 is the closing sentence. As in F20A, unit 8 avoids a segment-final bare German 'Protein' (which lsne.lang_id would label 'E') by using the genitive 'die Fehlfaltung des Proteins'; 'Bastian' is labelled 'N' by lsne.lang_id, which costs no accuracy because 'N' labels are excluded from the counts.
